install.title: Install Cartas on your phone
install.body: It opens like an app, starts faster, and the rules stay with you when the signal does not.
install.manual2: Choose “Install app” or “Add to Home Screen”.
install.accountTitle: With an account, or as a guest?
install.accountBody: With an account, your favourites and matches follow you to any phone. As a guest they stay on this one, and you can make the account whenever you like.
install.profileBody: If you said no earlier, it is here whenever you want it.
install.installed: Installed. Open it from your home screen.

auth.title: Sign in
auth.body: Sign in with your email and password, or make an account in a minute.
auth.notConfigured: No database is connected yet, so signing in is not possible. That is the next step.
auth.deleteConfirm: Sure? This deletes your account and everything of yours: favourites, decks, folders, groups, matches and messages. It cannot be undone.
auth.deleteKeeps: Games you published stay in the catalogue, without your name.

problem.rateLimit: Too many tries in a row. Wait a while and try again.
problem.invalidEmail: That email does not look right. Check the spelling.
problem.offline: The server could not be reached. Check your connection and try again.
problem.wrongLogin: The email or the password is not right.
problem.usernameTaken: There is already an account with that email. Sign in instead.
problem.weakPassword: That password is too short or too easy. Pick another.
problem.unknown: That did not work. If it happens again, send me the details.

auth.bodyPassword: Sign in with your email and password.
auth.signUpBody: Pick a handle, give your email, your date of birth and a password. There is nothing to verify.
auth.passwordMismatch: The two passwords do not match.
auth.password_common: That is one of the first passwords anybody would try. Pick another.
auth.haveAccount: Already have an account? Sign in
auth.noVerification: We send you nothing and there is nothing to confirm: creating the account signs you in. The email is only for signing in, and for recovering the password the day you need to.
auth.emailShape: Write the whole address, with an @ and a domain.
auth.handleNote: This is how friends see you and find you. You can change it later in your profile.
auth.emailNote: Your email is not published and does not appear on your profile.
auth.birthdateNote: Asked once, and only to know whether you can see adult games. It is not published, nobody else sees it, and the day you turn {{adult}} they unlock by themselves.
auth.birthdate_shape: That date does not make sense. Use the calendar.
auth.birthdate_future: That date is in the future.
auth.birthdate_tooYoung: You have to be at least {{min}} to make an account.
auth.birthdate_tooOld: That date is too far back. Have another look.
auth.forgotBody: Give your email and we will send a link to set a new one.
auth.forgotSent: If that address has an account, the link is on its way. Check the spam folder too.
auth.forgotWarning: The link opens in whichever browser your mail app prefers, which may not be this one. If that happens, come back here and sign in with the new password.
auth.backToSignIn: Back to signing in with my password
auth.newPasswordBody: Choose it and that is it. The old one is not needed.
auth.newPasswordNoLink: This link is no longer good: it has been used, or it expired, or it opened in another browser. Ask for another from the sign-in screen.

friends.needsAccount: Sign in with your email to have a friends list. People find you by your username, never by your email.
friends.noneYet: No friends yet. Search for them below by username.
friends.findHint: By name, not by email, so nobody can work out where you have an account. Type at least 2 letters.

folders.howToAdd: Empty. On any deck, tap “Add to a folder”.

profile.bad-characters: Lower case without accents, numbers and underscore only (no ñ, accents or spaces).
profile.noGames: You have not published a game yet. If you play something that is not here, write it up.

gameStatusNote.draft: Saved for you alone. It is in your searcher and you can play from it.
gameStatusNote.pending_review: I am reviewing it. While it waits it is still yours: it stays in your searcher and you can play from it. There is nothing for you to do.
gameStatusNote.published: Published: anyone can find it and play from it.
gameStatusNote.rejected: It did not go out. The reason is below: fix it and send it again.
gameStatusNote.archived: Archived. It no longer appears in the searcher.

profile.birthdateNote: This is what decides whether you see adult games. Asked once, and not changed.

failedWhat.matches: Your match history was not saved to your account.
failedWhat.both: Nothing could be saved to your account.

sync.failedBody: Nothing is lost: it is still on this device and it tries again as soon as you change something. If it does not clear, open the details.
sync.offline: No connection. You can carry on as normal — favourites, folders, matches — but changes are not saved to your account until the signal is back. Nothing is lost.

review.title: Games to review
review.intro: Every submitted game waits here, shown exactly as a reader will see it, so deciding is reading rather than digging.
review.empty: Nothing pending. When somebody submits a game, it shows up here.
review.notYours: This screen is for the owner account only.
review.reasonPlaceholder: What would have to change for this to be published…
review.reasonHint: The author sees this as written, and it is kept on the record. A rejection without a reason is refused.
review.reportByGone: Whoever reported it no longer has an account
review.takeDownPlaceholder: For example: the text is copied from a website.
review.takeDownHint: It stops being visible to everyone. The author keeps their copy and reads this reason on their profile. It is the only thing that undoes publishing.
review.actionFailed: That did not work. Try again.

editor.title: Publish a game
editor.intro: Five questions. You can save it half-written and come back another day.
editor.needsAccount: Sign in with your email to publish a game.
editor.summaryHint: A sentence or two: what it is. This is what shows under the name in the list.
editor.decksHint: Pick the deck and how many copies. Add a line if more than one kind is needed.
editor.missingHint: What happens if the deck is missing a card. The most appreciated thing you can say.
editor.missingNotePlaceholder: For example: the final count does not work without all forty cards.
editor.originalWording: I wrote these rules myself and did not copy the text from another site or a book.
editor.copyrightNote: Nobody owns the rules of a game: you may explain mus freely. The text somebody else wrote to explain them is theirs. Write it in your own words.
editor.adultOnly: This game is for adults (alcohol, money or adult themes).
editor.republishWarning: This game is already published. Submitting sends the changes to the review queue, and the version already approved stays visible meanwhile: nobody loses the game because you are editing it.

problem.title: The name has to be between 2 and 120 characters.
problem.summary: The summary needs between 10 and 600 characters. One sentence is enough.
problem.players: Players run from 1 to 64, and the maximum cannot be below the minimum.
problem.playersBest: “Best with” has to be between the minimum and the maximum.
problem.teamSize: You said it is played in teams: say how many to a team, between 2 and 8.
problem.decks: Pick the deck the game needs.
problem.duration: Duration runs from 1 to 1440 minutes, and the maximum cannot be below the minimum.
problem.sections: How it is played is missing: without that nobody can play it.
problem.originalWording: Tick the box saying the text is yours.
problem.tagline: The one-line summary cannot go over 160 characters.
problem.age: The minimum age has to be between 3 and 21. If anyone can play, leave it on “all ages”.
problem.deckQuantity: How many decks of the same kind: between 1 and 20.

editor.twoWays: Saving privately asks only for the name and the short description — the least needed to store it. Submitting also asks how it is played and which deck, and while it is reviewed the game is still yours: it stays in the searcher and you can play from it.
editor.privateOptionBody: Quick: the name and a sentence, and that is it. Leave the rest empty and finish another day. Nobody else sees it.
editor.publicOptionBody: It needs the name, the sentence, how it is played and which deck. It gets reviewed before it goes out, and you can use it meanwhile.
editor.privateNote: Saved for you alone. You will find it in your searcher and your profile, and you can make it public whenever you like.
editor.publicNote: Sending it puts it in the review queue. While it waits it is still yours: it stays in your searcher and you can play from it.
editor.ageHint: Leave it on “all ages” if there is no recommended one.

saveFailed.slugTaken: There is already a game with almost the same name. Change the name a little and try again.
saveFailed.notAllowed: You do not have permission to save this game. If it is someone else’s, make your own copy.
saveFailed.signedOut: Your session ended. Sign in again — what you wrote is still here.
saveFailed.offline: The server could not be reached. It may be your connection, a browser blocker, or the server not answering.
saveFailed.unknown: It could not be saved. If it happens again, open the technical details and send them to me.

editor.gameTitleHint: Whatever you call it at home. Between 2 and 120 characters.
editor.howToPlayHint: Tell it the way you would tell somebody who has just sat down at the table: what is dealt, what you do on your turn, and who wins.
editor.extraSectionsHint: Only if they add something. Anything left empty does not appear on the game page.
editor.needsHint: What has to be on the table before you can play.
editor.durationHint: In minutes. Leave it empty if you do not know.
editor.complexityHint: From 1 (learnt in a minute) to 5 (takes practice).
editor.notesHint: Optional. House variants, the usual mistakes, where the game comes from — whatever does not belong in the rules.

ai.intro: A card-games expert who explains a game another way, referees with the rules in front of it, or tells you what to play.

modeHint.explain: Re-explains a game however suits you: for a child, in a minute, or by walking through a sample hand.
modeHint.referee: Answers only from that game's published rules, and says when they do not cover it instead of inventing one.
modeHint.suggest: Recommends only games that exist here, with one concrete reason each.

placeholder.referee: We both played a seven at the same time — who wins the trick?
placeholder.suggest: Three of us, not much time, and one has never played.

ai.caveat: It is an AI and can be wrong. If it contradicts the published rules, the rules win.

problem.not-configured: No database is connected yet, so the expert cannot work.
problem.not-deployed: The expert is not deployed yet. It is written and ready: the function has to be uploaded and the key set (see supabase/functions/ai-expert/README.md).
problem.no-api-key: The Anthropic key is missing on the server. Set it with: supabase secrets set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=…
problem.sign-in-required: Sign in to use the expert.
problem.monthly-limit: You have reached this month's question limit. It resets on its own.
problem.game-not-found: That game is not published, so there are no rules to read.
problem.unknown: Something went wrong asking. Try again.

ai.soonBody: The expert is written and working underneath, but it is not switched on yet, so it cannot answer you for now. We would rather tell you than leave you a screen that always fails.
ai.soonMeanwhile: In the meantime, every game has its full rules on its own page, with a jump list for finding the bit you need in the middle of a game.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.intro: What this app keeps, who can see it, and how to make it go away. No small print.

whatWeKeep.title: What is kept
whatWeKeep.body: Your email, so you can sign in. Your username and the name others see. What you star, the decks you say you own, your folders, your groups, the matches you play with their notes, and the messages you write in a group. Nothing else: no ads, no tracking, nothing shared with third parties.

whatIsPublic.title: What anyone can see
whatIsPublic.body: Your username and display name, because that is how friends find you, and any games you publish, with your name as the author. Nobody sees your email: it is not even stored in the profile table that can be queried.

whatIsPrivate.title: What is only yours
whatIsPrivate.body: Your favourites, decks, folders, matches, settings and your groups' chats. The database enforces it rather than a promise: every table has rules that stop another person reading your rows, and automated tests check them.

where.title: Where it lives
where.body: In Supabase, on Amazon servers in Frankfurt (European Union). The app itself is served from Vercel, which only hands over the page: it stores none of your data.

ai.title: The AI expert
ai.body: If you use the expert, your question and the rules of the game you are asking about are sent to Anthropic to produce the answer. Your email, your name and your matches are not. If you do not use that screen, nothing is sent to anybody.

howLong.title: How long
howLong.body: Until you delete it. There is no expiry and no automatic clear-out.

deleting.title: Deleting everything
deleting.body: Your profile has a button to delete the account. It really deletes: your email, profile, favourites, decks, folders, groups, matches and messages, and whatever the app kept on this device. The only thing that stays is any game you published, without your name, because those are rules other people are using.

children.title: Minors
children.body: Games marked 18+ warn before they open and can be hidden from your profile. Nobody is asked for a date of birth: it would prove nothing and would be one more piece of your data kept for no reason.

contact.title: Questions
contact.body: Write to [put your contact email here] and I will answer.
